subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 7: English in action – Asking and saying what you prefer
outcomes: Ask and say what you prefer with Would you rather / I'd prefer to.
Use correct stress in sentences with 'd.
Make sentences about past events with after + Past perfect.

tf.s: 'Would you rather go caving or abseiling?' asks about a preference.
tf.why: Yes, 'Would you rather...?' asks what someone prefers.
After prefer we need to: I'd prefer to go hiking.
Correct, 'd is short for had here.

tf.s: On day two of the holiday, Frank chooses diving.
tf.why: Frank chooses hiking because he is a bit scared of going underwater; Lucas chooses diving.

tf.s: Lucas and Frank choose abseiling on day three.
tf.why: Right, they both choose abseiling on day three.

tf.s: In Past perfect sentences, the main verb is usually stressed.
tf.why: Yes, we stress the main verb, like 'finished'.

tf.s: The short form 'd is strongly stressed.
tf.why: 'd is not stressed; the main verb is stressed.

tf.s: 'Should we go snorkelling or surfing?' is a way to suggest two choices.
tf.why: Good, 'Should we ... or ...?' offers two options.
We say 'I'd rather go', with no 'to'.

tf.s: Lucas and Frank are talking about their adventure holiday.
tf.why: Yes, they plan activities for their adventure holiday.

boxes.q: Complete: ___ you rather go caving or abseiling?
boxes.why: We ask preferences with 'Would you rather...?'

boxes.q: Complete: Would you prefer ___ go diving or caving?

boxes.why: I'd rather + verb: I'd rather go hiking.

boxes.q: What does Frank prefer on day two?
boxes.why: Frank prefers hiking on day two.

boxes.q: Why doesn't Frank want to go diving?
o: He is scared of going underwater.
boxes.why: Frank is a bit scared of going underwater.

boxes.q: What do the boys do on day one?
boxes.why: Day one's activity is horse riding.

boxes.q: In 'After he'd finished his game', which word is stressed?
boxes.why: The main verb 'finished' takes the stress.

boxes.q: What does Lucas choose on day two?
boxes.why: Lucas chooses diving on day two.

boxes.q: Which phrase gives your opinion about a plan?
boxes.why: 'I think we should...' gives your opinion.

boxes.q: Continue: After our alarms had gone off, ...
boxes.why: The later action uses the Past simple: we got up.

mcq.q: Which question asks about a preference?
o: Would you rather watch the sunrise or the sunset?
mcq.why: 'Would you rather...?' asks someone to choose.

mcq.q: What are Lucas and Frank talking about?
mcq.why: They are choosing adventure holiday activities.

mcq.q: What do Lucas and Frank choose on day three?
mcq.why: They choose abseiling on day three.

mcq.q: Which part of a Past perfect sentence with 'd is NOT stressed?
mcq.why: The short form 'd is weak and not stressed.

mcq.q: Your friend asks: 'Would you prefer to go skateboarding or surfboarding?' Choose the best answer.
Ask about lunch: pizza or sandwiches?
o: Would you rather take pizza or sandwiches for lunch?
Would you rather to take pizza or sandwiches?
Do you rather pizza or sandwiches?
Would you prefer take pizza or sandwiches?

mcq.q: Join: We ate our breakfast. We showered.
o: After we had eaten our breakfast, we showered.
After we ate our breakfast, we had showered.
After we have eaten breakfast, we shower.
After we had eat our breakfast, we showered.
mcq.why: The first action uses the Past perfect: had eaten.

mcq.q: Why does Frank choose hiking on day two?
o: He is a bit scared of going underwater.
mcq.why: His fear of going underwater makes him choose hiking.

mcq.q: Lucas and Frank choose different things on day two. What does this show?
mcq.why: Asking about preferences helps friends plan when they want different things.

mcq.q: 'After we'd watched the sunset, we went to bed.' Which words are stressed?
mcq.why: Main verbs and important nouns are stressed; small words like 'd are weak.
